before_notes: Activated by the owner-approved Gamma 601 F4 plan (delightful-foraging-quill, F4.6) under the linked parity plan to propose this row's status from committed Gamma 601 evidence; no device effect is authorized.
after_notes: On the Gamma 601, the TPS546 output is commanded and confirmed off through the safe boot. A bounded test-build check wrote its 32-register configuration with every readback matching, held 1144 to 1146 mV at a 1.15 V target for 60 s with no faults, and confirmed the output off again; see docs/parity/evidence/20261023-gamma601-vout-check.md. Its VIN, IOUT and regulator temperature then fed the safety limits through local mining, the 4-hour soak, the self-test and the production smoke soak (regulator peak 80.0 C, in the 4-hour soak), and a test build's overheat restart ran at 1050 mV. The promoted production build runs the same configuration and enable path. Two deliberate deviations bound the voltage: VOUT_COMMAND is written at the target and VOUT_MAX is 1.25 V, under a 1.20 V target cap. See docs/parity/work-plans/20261029T040602Z-PWR-004/RESULT.md. Live voltage changes are deferred on the 601 (ADR-0041 item 15). A regulator overheat ends the run stopped rather than recovering as upstream does (ADR-0041 item 11). The 105 C regulator throttle, injected faults, the output state from power-on until the safe boot's off write and after a panic, analog accuracy, other voltages and other TPS546 boards remain non-claims.
